sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in the React type for drawings and the sport key type from the landing content file.
sections.why: Likely reason: the type keeps the sport names the same as the content file.

sections.name: line
sections.title: Shared outline style
sections.what: Sets one common outline style for every icon: thin rounded lines, no fill, drawn in the current text colour.
sections.why: Likely reason: a shared style keeps the five icons looking like one family.
sections.watch_out: The stroke width is set once here, so changing it changes every outline icon at the same time.

sections.name: SHAPES
sections.title: Drawings for each sport
sections.what: Holds one drawing for each of the five sports: cricket, basketball, football, an F1 car and tennis. Each is built from simple lines and filled dots.
sections.why: The file comment says the style follows the Munich 1972 Olympic pictograms.
sections.watch_out: Every sport key needs a drawing here; the type check enforces this, so a new sport needs its icon added too.

sections.name: Pictogram
sections.title: Icon wrapper
sections.what: Places the chosen drawing inside a square image box that screen readers skip. The landing cards and tiles use it.
sections.why: Likely reason: the icons are decoration, so they are hidden from assistive tools.
sections.watch_out: A sport name missing from the drawing list gives an empty box rather than an error.

summary: Draws the small sport icon (cricket, basketball, football, F1, tennis) used on the landing page, and hides it from screen readers because it is decoration only.
purpose: Give each analyst a recognisable sport symbol without loading image files.
why: The icons are drawn in code so they stay sharp at any size and need no image downloads. Reason for hiding them from screen readers: the file comment calls them decorative, so they add no information.
how: 1) The landing page passes in a sport key. 2) The component looks up the matching drawing. 3) It wraps the drawing in an image box that screen readers skip, and returns it.
inputs: A sport key (one of five values) and an optional class name for sizing.
outputs: An SVG image element showing the chosen sport drawing.
risks: An unknown sport key gives an empty box with no warning. The component handles no user data.
debug: If an icon is blank, check that the sport key matches an entry in the drawing list in this file and in the landing content. If the size is wrong, check the class name passed in from Landing.
